claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a relatively homogeneous, single-phase microstructure.
Annealing at approximately 700°C for 1 hour in an inert atmosphere promotes selective Cu segregation.
The specified annealing treatment avoids gross microstructural coarsening.
Annealing produces a continuous or semi-continuous Cu-rich layer along grain boundaries and in near-surface regions.
Cu has a lower enthalpy of mixing in the FeNiCrCoCu matrix.
The annealing treatment drives Cu segregation toward interfaces.
The segregated Cu-rich phase is lubricious and thermally stable in the intended operating regime.
The Cu-rich interfacial phase lowers the friction coefficient during sliding.
The Cu-rich interfacial phase reduces stress concentrations.
Reduced stress concentrations produce a more uniform distribution of plastic deformation.
More uniform plastic deformation improves wear resistance.
Relative to the as-deposited coating, the annealed coating will have a lower friction coefficient during high-temperature sliding.
Relative to the as-deposited coating, the annealed coating will have a lower wear rate during high-temperature sliding.
Relative to the as-deposited coating, the annealed coating will exhibit less localized microscopic deformation, including finer and more distributed deformation bands.
The proposed beneficial mechanism should operate during sliding at approximately 550–650°C under constant load and sliding speed.
In the 550–650°C regime, thermally activated diffusion enables Cu segregation without detrimental coarsening or loss of coating adhesion.
Outside the 550–650°C regime or after overly aggressive annealing, the proposed benefits may not occur.
